params._roi_note: start_x/start_y centre the 32x32 ROI on the beam parked at coarse bias 2/2 (fine 1.5/2.15): probe-verified 2026-07-21, full-sensor CoM (x 919, y 507). Re-derive with contrib/calibration-scripts/configurations/probe_frame.json only if the alignment (not the bias) changes -- the ROI now follows the beam by cropping instead of re-biasing.

pipeline._note1: THE TEST. Sits after the CoM sinks (watchers see the true error) and before the FSP. pass_open=true: open phase feeds the FSP the REAL error (not zeros) so it can identify while its own start_delay hold (600 s, see fsp params) keeps its command at zero -- the DAC still parks at bias throughout, only fsp's internal view of the error changes. settle_time covers FSP/NLMS/adapt re-convergence after closure. pixel_scale 15.5 = (32-1)/2 for the 32x32 ROI. 500/500 @ nfft 4096 matches attenuation_fsp15 (run 15) for a SHARED frequency grid -> directly comparable closed RMS.

params._pass_open: 2026-07-27: pass the real open-loop error through to fsp instead of zeros (default false). fsp is a predictive controller with its own matched start_delay hold (see fsp start_delay below) -- without this it identified on 500 s of fabricated zeros and only started learning live once real error arrived at t=600s, already at full authority with no ramp.
params.config:
ATTENUATION 21 -- two-timescale FSP plus transient recovery, based on the verified attenuation20 operating point.
Camera/CoM: 32x32 ROI start_x 1025 / start_y 492, exposure 125, gain 100, bw 100, 20x20 tracked window thr 22; coarse bias 2/2 (offset [2,2,2,2]).
FSP: broad_order 512, broad_mu .03, broad_lp 11; drift_tau 2 s separates slow pointing from vibration prediction. Large-event recovery triggers at max(6 sigma, 0.03 normalized), preserves drift correction, uses bounded Kp=.25 feedback, holds 0.1 s quiet, then cross-fades to prediction over 0.25 s; learning freezes during recovery.
Delay per-axis y 5+0.828 / x 6+0 (full-band bode phase 07-21 PM); K y 0.645 / x 0.803 (full-band bode plateau, <=30 Hz); adapt_period 8 adapt_tau 5.
Guard: ON (guard_ratio 4, defaults) -- re-enabled 2026-07-27 now that pass_open lets fsp identify on real open-loop data before closing (see attenuation_test's pass_open), rather than compensating for that gap by running without burst protection. Stall-gap patch ON. Run under perf-mode with the established chrt/taskset settings.
COMPARE against attenuation20 and attenuation_fsp15: report total and per-band closed RMS, 60-400 Hz waterbed, command/clamp behavior, and transient activation count. Same 500/500/4096 grid. refs: Kulcsar 2006 / Petit 2008 / Meimon 2010 / Correia 2010

pipeline._note1: THE CONTROLLER. Delay is measured from the BODE PHASE, not the departure latency: departure latency (delay=4+.02, 1.061 ms) under-modeled the delay by 1.6-2.3 frames and left a near-unity command-echo residual around 300 Hz; the 2026-07-16 20:55 run spiraled at ~310 Hz once the ramp passed ~50% authority. The 2026-07-16 full-band (5-300 Hz) phase-slope fit (fsm_bodex/y_716, x 5.62 fr / y 6.37 fr at 3788 Hz) established the method and first set a global delay=6+0.0. THAT MEASUREMENT IS SUPERSEDED: the delay actually configured below is per-axis, from the 2026-07-21 PM full-band re-fit at the re-centred operating point (see the _delay note) -- global/x stays 6+0.0, y is now the override 5+0.828. broad_order=512 and broad_mu=.03 match attenuation11.
pipeline._note2: K is the SIGNED command->error gain (error units per command unit). CURRENT values (see each axis's _K) are the 2026-07-21 PM full-band bode plateaus at the re-centred operating point: Ky=0.645, Kx=0.803, both sign +. These supersede the 2026-07-20 latency step-gains (Kx=0.641/Ky=0.562 at bias 1.2/2.45) and the older bode plateaus at the 1.98/1.97 bias (Kx=0.902/Ky=0.621) -- K is bias-dependent and shifts with every re-centre, NOT because the units changed. Bode-era context: CoM units are normalized to the frame half-width, so the 32px-ROI plateaus are DOUBLE the 64px-era 0.434/0.315. K too SMALL means commands too STRONG (u=-cancel/K); verify the push-test sign and watch the burst guard on the first closed run after any bias/ROI move.
pipeline._note3: With broad_order>0 the identified full-band observer supplies the command and the AR2 modal estimate is not added, avoiding double cancellation. The modal q/r values remain available for diagnostics and for rollback with broad_order=0. broad_mu is the NLMS identification step: lower it if weights are noisy, raise it only if the disturbance spectrum changes faster than the current observer converges.
pipeline._note4: zeta ~0.002 = sharp line; ~0.3 = broadband hump. adapt_period>0 turns on Petit/Meimon re-identification: every 8 s it refreshes each mode's q from its recent energy, r from the innovation floor, nudges center frequencies toward the measured lines (capped at adapt_df_max Hz/update, matching the ~0.5 Hz/run wander), and recomputes the Kalman gain. Set adapt_period 0 for a fixed FSP while first validating.

params._delay: 2026-07-21 PM PERFECTLY-ACCURATE per-axis delay from the FULL-BAND (5-300 Hz) bode phase slope at the re-centred operating point (coarse 2/2, ROI 904/492, exp 150): x tau 1.325 ms => 5.995 fr (fsm_bodex_721_full, fs 3769); y tau 1.284 ms => 5.828 fr (fsm_bodey_721_full, fs 3761); +1 hidden frame already included. Cross-checked vs the latency 50%-crossing (x 5.9 / y 6.0) -- agree within 0.15 fr, trusted. Set PER-AXIS: global/x = 6+0.0, y override = 5+0.828 (see y block). The 30-Hz-capped bode could NOT resolve tau (too little phase over 5-30 Hz -> bogus 4.98); this full-band sweep is the long-owed measurement. departure floor x4.0/y5.0 fr, NEVER used (too short caused the 07-16 310 Hz spiral).
params._broad_lp: 2026-07-22 observer band-limit, synced from steering_fsp.json (see its _broad_lp note): 11-tap boxcar prefilter on the NLMS input kills the 300-420 Hz command-echo regeneration (the 380 Hz x limit cycle) at the root; +5 frames folded into the broad horizon, in-band timing unchanged.
params._broad_freeze_closed: 2026-07-27: restored to true (the default) now that attenuation_test passes real open-loop error through (pass_open) for the full 500 s open phase. Identification happens during the start_delay hold on genuine data; freezing on close (per doc/devices/fsp.md) avoids closed-loop NLMS learning leaked command as disturbance. Previously false only because pass_open was missing and there was no real data to learn from except live.
params._two_timescale: ATTENUATION21: slow drift is cancelled by a separate EWMA state; NLMS/modal observers see only the vibration residual. Large prediction innovations temporarily select bounded proportional recovery while preserving the drift command, freeze learning, then cross-fade back.
params._start_delay: 2026-07-27: = attenuation_test start_delay(100) + open_time(500), so fsp's own hold spans the ENTIRE recorded open phase (now real data, via pass_open) instead of closing at its own t~30s while attenuation_test still zeroes the input. Previously 20 -- wrong: fsp fully closed hundreds of seconds before real error ever reached it.
params._ramp: unchanged: 10 s starting at t=600 lands the bumpless handover well inside attenuation_test's 120 s settle_time, so full authority is reached long before the closed-loop recording window (t=720-1220) starts.
params._guard: burst guard (2026-07-17, on by default): the run-15 rerun showed intermittent ~250-450 Hz ring bursts (regeneration at fs/(2*delay) when K/delay drift off the plant, e.g. after a coarse-bias move) that tripled the closed RMS. Per-axis band-pass detector on the raw error at the regeneration freq fs/(2*(delay+delay_frac)) -- at THIS run's per-axis delays that's ~325 Hz y (delay 5.828) / ~316 Hz x (delay 6.0); on a burst the axis's authority is cut to 0 for guard_hold s, NLMS training and adaptation stats freeze, then authority ramps back over guard_ramp s. Trigger = band envelope > guard_ratio x max(learned quiet baseline, guard_floor). A ticker prints the activation count every guard_tick s. Recurring activations = re-measure K/delay at the current bias.
params._guard_history: 2026-07-21 PM this was set to 0 (burst detector OFF) in steering_fsp.json after the 316/344 Hz detector false-tripped on low-frequency leakage post y-re-centre (x error 99.6% below 30 Hz, no real HF regeneration, yet cutting x authority every ~1.25 s and manufacturing 'random spikes' up to 4.75 px). That value was inherited here unexamined. Restored to the default 4 on 2026-07-27: this harness's K/delay are freshly bode-fit (see per-axis _K/_delay notes) and pass_open now gives fsp real data to identify from before it closes, so the burst guard is doing its intended job (catching genuine K/delay-mismatch regeneration) rather than standing in for a broken hold. If it starts false-tripping on leakage again, the real fix is a higher-Q / sustained-energy detector (not the floor), per the note this run's config left for that case.

y._K: 2026-07-21 PM full-band bode plateau at the re-centred operating point (fsm_bodey_721_full, 5-300 Hz, K from <=30 Hz): Ky=0.645 +/-0.005 err-units/minmax cmd, sign +, LINEAR (robust median 2.5%). DOWN from the pre-recentre 0.679 (K is position/bias-dependent; re-centring y shifted it); matches the latency step median 0.656. K is bias-dependent.
y._delay: y OWN full-band delay: bode tau 1.284 ms => 5.828 fr (fs 3761), latency 50%-cross 6.0 -- set 5+0.828, slightly shorter than x's 6.00 (which x inherits from the global).

x._K: 2026-07-21 PM full-band bode plateau at the re-centred operating point (fsm_bodex_721_full, 5-300 Hz, K from <=30 Hz): Kx=0.803 +/-0.006 err-units/minmax cmd, sign +, LINEAR -- confirms the earlier 30-Hz 0.805. Full-band |H| flatness 5.6% (the x resonance ~130 Hz is now in-band, above crossover). The FSP corrects small jitter (<<0.2) = small-signal regime; the latency large-step gain was only 0.622 (x COMPRESSES at large drive), but small-signal is the right one and the safe (gentler) direction. x delay = the global 6+0.0 (full-band tau 1.325 ms => 5.995 fr).
